input_only_rival_source:
def nearest_frame_only(grid: Grid, *, frame_wins_ties: bool) -> Grid:
    """Reflect only when the target is nearest to blue, using input pixels only.

    This is the independent counterpart of the generic nearest-component label
    mutations on this task's one-frame manifold. No measured output is read.
    """
    out = copy.deepcopy(grid)
    r1, c1, r2, c2 = _frame(grid)
    marks = [(r, c) for r, row in enumerate(grid) for c, value in enumerate(row)
             if value == 4 and r1 < r < r2 and c1 < c < c2]
    for r, c in marks:
        target = c1 + c2 - c
        if grid[r][target] != 0:
            continue
        blue_distance = min(r - r1, r2 - r, target - c1, c2 - target)
        yellow_distance = min(abs(r - rr) + abs(target - cc) for rr, cc in marks)
        if blue_distance < yellow_distance or (frame_wins_ties and blue_distance == yellow_distance):
            out[r][target] = 7
    return out

repair_constraints.primary_row: At least two cells from both horizontal frame borders.
repair_constraints.primary_column: One column from the integer frame axis.
repair_constraints.proof: The empty mirror target has yellow distance1 and blue distance>=2, strictly refuting both nearest-frame rivals.
repair_constraints.rotation_redundancy: Both odd draws in every four consecutive draws contain the witness; removing one leaves one.
repair_constraints.collision: Try both primary orientations: when the global/frame axis sums differ by1, one global preimage is the required center yellow.
repair_constraints.override_policy: Keep explicit overrides outside these extra teaching constraints.
